opus.why: Mechanical version bump across a few known files. Medium effort so it actually searches every CI workflow and doesn't miss one.

fable.why: Mechanical version bump across three named files; just needs to grep for node version pins and edit them without touching anything else.

opus.why: Standard lockfile-drift diagnosis: the lockfile wasn't committed after the vite bump, or local and CI pnpm versions differ. Needs a clear explanation and a fix that doesn't use no-frozen-lockfile, but no deep reasoning.

fable.why: Well-known pnpm error with the cause in the log: package.json was bumped without regenerating/committing the lockfile, local install silently updates it. Explain, run pnpm install, commit lockfile; high effort to honor the no-frozen-lockfile constraint and check git state.

opus.why: Well-known pattern: multi-stage Gradle to JRE build, dependency-layer caching, non-root user, maybe layered jars. Sonnet at high gets the details right.

fable.why: Multi-stage Gradle/Spring Boot Dockerfile with dependency-layer caching (copy wrapper+build files first), non-root user, slim JRE runtime image; standard pattern but caching the Gradle dependency step correctly takes some care.

opus.why: Script that deletes files on a schedule. The KEEP and age logic, logging and Task Scheduler registration must be correct and safe. Not architecturally hard, but mistakes are costly, so high effort.

fable.why: PowerShell cleanup script plus scheduled task registration with logging; routine, but it deletes data on a production render machine, so age semantics and the KEEP guard must be right and a dry-run mode is expected.

opus.why: Design a single schema with collected errors, per-env overrides and an .env.example generator. Moderate design work that Sonnet at high handles well.

fable.why: Small design task: zod-style schema with required/optional vars, per-env overrides, aggregated missing-var errors, and a generator that derives .env.example from the schema. Sonnet handles this well at high effort.

opus.why: Zero-downtime blue/green deploy on production: nginx switching, healthchecks, rollback, and compose port/state handling. Architectural, high-stakes, with many ways to fail subtly.

fable.why: Infra architecture: blue/green on a single VPS with compose, nginx upstream switch after healthcheck, image tagging so rollback works, DB shared across both. Many subtle failure modes where a mediocre design silently keeps downtime or breaks rollback.

opus.why: Follow-up fix for a known GitLab limitation: cache paths must sit inside the project dir, so set GRADLE_USER_HOME under CI_PROJECT_DIR and adjust the key. The log points straight at the cause.

fable.why: Log states the cause: cache paths must be relative to the project dir. Fix is GRADLE_USER_HOME under CI_PROJECT_DIR and matching cache paths, plus noting the runner has no shared cache. Known GitLab pattern.

opus.why: Standard tooling setup: uv, ruff, pre-commit, and a cross-platform task runner. Convention-driven work that only needs care about Windows/mac parity.

fable.why: Repo tooling migration (uv pyproject, ruff, pre-commit) with a cross-platform task runner choice since make is not native on Windows; needs judgment on the runner and faithful migration of the 12 deps.

opus.why: Helm-optional CronJob reusing an existing secret, S3 retention, and a Prometheus alert for two consecutive failures, which is tricky with kube-state-metrics. Several systems together, and getting it wrong means silently losing backups.

fable.why: Multi-part k8s/Helm work: conditional CronJob, pg_dump to S3 with retention, reuse of an existing secret, and a PromQL rule for two consecutive failures, which is subtle with kube-state-metrics job metrics. Silent backup failure is costly, so correctness matters.
